observation.visible_scene: A container port at twilight/night, viewed across a body of water. A large gantry/ship-to-shore crane stands center-frame with its boom raised diagonally up-left; a second crane and a container-laden ship sit at the left edge. Rows of multicolored shipping containers line the quay, lit by numerous bright floodlights, including one tall pole light on the right. The foreground shows calm water with vertical light reflections and a low concrete wall covered in graffiti. The sky is a deep blue with a faint purple band near the horizon.
visible_changes: The overall composition is static across the entire excerpt: the central crane's boom angle, the left crane, the ship, the container stacks, and the floodlight positions all remain in the same frame locations from t=0.000 to t=1.333s.
No camera pan, tilt, or zoom is evident; background elements (right-hand tall light pole, graffiti wall edges) hold constant positions relative to the frame.

The only perceptible variation is subtle shimmering/softening of the bright vertical reflections on the water surface and minor flicker around the floodlight halos, consistent with gentle water motion rather than object movement.
No part of the crane structure (boom, trolley, legs) translates or rotates; no containers or ships change position.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the crane was moving before this segment or begins operating after it (the boom stays raised and idle throughout the crop).
Any longer-term lighting, sky, or tide changes beyond the 1.33s window.
Whether the ship or any vehicles move outside this excerpt.
uncertain_details: Whether the slight changes in water-reflection streaks are real ripples or video-compression noise.
Whether the purple horizon band drifts imperceptibly or is constant.
Exact cause of any minor halo flicker on the floodlights (atmosphere vs. encoding).
